user: I don't enjoy games with pixel art graphics.
assistant:  That's completely fine! Everyone has different preferences when it comes to the types of games they enjoy. Some people prefer games with realistic graphics, while others enjoy the retro aesthetic of pixel art. It's important to find the types of games that you enjoy and that make you happy.

If you're not a fan of pixel art graphics, there are plenty of other games out there with different styles of graphics that you might enjoy. You could try exploring different genres or looking for games with more modern or realistic graphics.

Additionally, it's worth noting that not all pixel art games are created equal. Some pixel art games have very basic graphics, while others have highly detailed and intricate designs. If you're not a fan of pixel art in general, it might be worth giving a few different pixel art games a try to see if there are any that you enjoy despite the graphics.

Ultimately, the most important thing is to find games that you enjoy playing, regardless of the type of graphics they have.

user: 3.Question 3Consider the following user story: “As a plant owner, I want to learn from other, more experienced plant owners so that I can better care for my plant.”Which of the following pieces of acceptance criteria are appropriate for this story? Select all that apply.1 pointAbility to join a mailing list Ability to access an “Expert Advice” section on the websiteAbility to join an online discussion group for trading plant care tipsAbility to sign up for Q&A sessions with plant experts
assistant: The appropriate acceptance criteria for this user story are:

•Ability to join an online discussion group for trading plant care tips 
•Ability to sign up for Q&A sessions with plant experts

These choices align well with the goal of learning from more experienced plant owners in order to better care for the user's plant.

The other options, while potentially useful features, do not directly address learning from interactive discussions with expert plant owners.

So I would select:

Ability to join an online discussion group for trading plant care tips
Ability to sign up for Q&A sessions with plant experts

user: 4.Question 4Which of the following user stories is complete and follows the correct structure?1 point“I want to purchase plants, but I’m worried they won’t get to me safely.”“I want to order plant care tools so that I can keep my plants healthy.”“As a plant owner, I want to know how much sunlight my plant needs so that I can maximize its growth.”“As a customer, I want to be able to access my account dashboard quickly and easily.”
assistant: The user story that is complete and follows the correct structure is:

“As a plant owner, I want to know how much sunlight my plant needs so that I can maximize its growth.”

This story follows the standard user story structure:

As a [role], I want [goal/desire] so that [benefit].

The other options are missing either the role, goal/desire, or benefit. The full list with issues:

“I want to purchase plants, but I’m worried they won’t get to me safely.” - Missing role and benefit 
“I want to order plant care tools so that I can keep my plants healthy.” - Missing role
“As a customer, I want to be able to access my account dashboard quickly and easily.” - Benefit is not strongly tied to the goal/desire

So the correct choice is:

“As a plant owner, I want to know how much sunlight my plant needs so that I can maximize its growth.”

assistant: The user stories that could lead to a discussion group or live chat option are:

“As a plant expert, I want to connect with other customers so that I can discuss plant care tips and tricks.”  
“As a plant owner, I want to get expert help and advice quickly so that I know what to do if my plant gets sick.”

These stories express a desire for interactive communication with other plant owners and experts, which could be addressed through discussion forums, live chat, or other real-time options.

The other options focus more on purchasing plants or plant products, rather than connecting with a community.

So the correct choices are:  

“As a plant expert, I want to connect with other customers so that I can discuss plant care tips and tricks.”

The option "As a plant owner, I only want to purchase rare succulents but Virtual Verde does not offer any." could potentially lead to a discussion group for locating hard to find plants, but the story as written is focused specifically on unavailable products rather than community interaction.

user: 1.Question 1As a Product Owner building a Backlog, what pieces of information should you include for each item? Select all that apply.1 pointThe level of effort required to complete the itemA clear description from the perspective of the customerThe date the item is dueA set value for the item, such as dollar signs
assistant: The pieces of information that should be included for each item in a product backlog are:

•A clear description from the perspective of the customer
•The level of effort required to complete the item 

These choices provide the necessary information for the team to understand what needs to be built and how much work is involved.

The date the item is due and a set value are not needed in the initial product backlog. Dates and estimates can be added later during sprint planning and refinement. The backlog simply needs enough detail for the team to understand the user need and level of effort.

So the correct choices are:

A clear description from the perspective of the customer
The level of effort required to complete the item

The options "The date the item is due" and "A set value for the item, such as dollar signs" should not be selected.

user: 2.Question 2A Product Owner writing a user story needs the story to fit within the planned Sprint. If the user story is too large, they break it down into multiple scaled-down stories to meet which of the I.N.V.E.S.T. story writing criteria?1 pointIndependentNegotiableValuableSmall
assistant: The I.N.V.E.S.T. criteria that addresses breaking down a large user story into multiple smaller stories is:

NAME_1

The "S" in I.N.V.E.S.T. stands for NAME_1, meaning that user stories should be NAME_1 enough to implement within an iteration. If a story is too big, it should be split into multiple smaller stories that still provide value.

The other options do not directly relate to the size and scope of user stories:

Independent - Stories should be independent of each other, but this does not address size 
Negotiable - The details of stories can be negotiated, but again does not address size
Valuable - Stories must provide value to the end user, but does not specify that stories should be NAME_1

So the correct choice is:

NAME_1

The Product Owner is splitting the larger user story into multiple "scaled-down stories" in order to meet the "NAME_1" criteria and fit the stories into the planned Sprint.

user: 3.Question 3Which effort estimation technique involves team members walking around the room and placing stickers on each item?1 pointDot VotingAffinity MappingThe Bucket SystemPlanning Poker™
assistant: The effort estimation technique that involves team members walking around and placing stickers on items is:

Dot Voting

Dot Voting, also known as sticker voting, has team members place dots or stickers on product backlog items to vote on their relative effort. The items with the most dots are considered the highest effort.

The other options do not involve sticking dots or stickers to items:

Affinity Mapping - Grouping related items together
The Bucket System - Assigning items to buckets of relative size/effort 
Planning PokerTM - Using cards to vote on effort, but does not involve sticking dots to items

So the correct choice is:

Dot Voting

Dot Voting has team members place physical dots or stickers on product backlog items during an estimation session. The other techniques listed are different methods of collaborative estimation.

user: 4.Question 4How much time exists between Sprints for a Scrum team?1 pointTwo daysOne monthZero daysOne week
assistant: For a Scrum team, the time between Sprints is:

Zero days

In Scrum, teams proceed immediately from one Sprint to the next. There is no gap between Sprints. The team reviews the recently completed Sprint, holds a retrospective, and plans the next Sprint without interruption. 

The other options indicate gaps between Sprints, which is not part of the Scrum framework:

Two days - Having a two day gap between Sprints would disrupt the flow and cadence of work 
One month - A month-long gap would go against the iterative and incremental nature of Scrum
One week - Scrum teams proceed continuously without week-long gaps between Sprints

So the correct choice is:

Zero days

Scrum teams move directly from the end of one Sprint into planning for the next Sprint with no time off in between. Sprints run with continuous increments and iterations as the team builds the product.

user: 5.Question 5Which of the following is a key deliverable of Sprint Planning?1 pointA burndown chartThe Sprint BacklogRetrospective notesThe project charter
assistant: The key deliverable of Sprint Planning is:

The Sprint Backlog

The purpose of Sprint Planning is for the team to define the Sprint Backlog - the body of work they will complete during the upcoming Sprint. They determine how much of the Product Backlog they can commit to based on their historical velocity.

The other options are not direct outputs or deliverables of Sprint Planning:

A burndown chart - Created to track progress during the Sprint, not an output of planning 
Retrospective notes - Produced at the end of the Sprint, not during planning
The project charter - Created before development begins, not an output of Sprint Planning

So the correct choice is:

The Sprint Backlog 

The Sprint Backlog, containing the Product Backlog items the team has committed to for the upcoming Sprint, is the primary deliverable resulting from the Sprint Planning meeting.

user: 6.Question 6Which role is responsible for assisting team members in clearing obstacles and unblocking their work? 1 pointScrum MasterProduct OwnerAnother teammateKey stakeholder
assistant: The role responsible for assisting team members in clearing obstacles and unblocking their work is:

Scrum Master

The Scrum Master serves the team by helping them remove impediments and facilitating their self-organization. Clearing blockers and enabling progress is a key responsibility of the Scrum Master role.

The other options do not describe this facilitation responsibility:

Product Owner - Responsible for the product roadmap and backlog, not removing impediments
Another teammate - While teammates should support each other, the Scrum Master role specifically focuses on unblocking the team 
Key stakeholder - Stakeholders provide input and feedback but do not directly assist in clearing obstacles

So the correct choice is:

Scrum Master

The Scrum Master helps resolve blockers, facilitate meetings, and enable the team's progress toward their goals. Removing obstacles and unblocking team members is a primary way the Scrum Master serves the team.
